title: Second hyperscaler names a non-Nvidia data-center inference-silicon partner by Q4 2027
body: Qualcomm's June 24 Dragonfly data-center roadmap did something its prior server-silicon pushes never managed: it attached a named hyperscaler, with Meta committing to the Dragonfly C1000 CPU for its next-generation server fleet at the part's 2028 commercial availability, alongside a Dragonfly AI300 inference accelerator and a High Bandwidth Compute memory tier pitched explicitly at Nvidia's inference economics. The named-customer reference, not the silicon specs, is the competitive trigger: once one hyperscaler is on the record backing a merchant non-Nvidia inference stack, the inference-economics argument moves from vendor marketing to a peer-validated procurement signal that rival cloud operators must answer. The prediction is that a second top-tier hyperscaler (among Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Oracle, Meta, or a comparable named operator distinct from Meta) will publicly commit to a named non-Nvidia data-center CPU or inference-accelerator partner — whether Qualcomm, AMD, a merchant rival, or its own custom-silicon arm announced as a named external design win — within a concrete window. The forcing function is that inference cost-per-token is now the dominant data-center economic line as agentic workloads scale, and no hyperscaler can let a competitor lock in a cheaper inference floor unanswered.

summary: Qualcomm's Dragonfly roadmap named Meta as its first data-center CPU customer, turning the inference-economics attack on Nvidia into a peer-validated procurement signal. With inference cost-per-token now the dominant cloud economic line, expect a second top-tier hyperscaler to publicly commit to a named non-Nvidia data-center CPU or inference-accelerator partner by Q4 2027.
